title: Monitoring Infrastructure
summary: Interpret synthetic telemetry for temperature, utilization, storage, power, and network status.
objectives: Distinguish normal, warning, and critical labels within a defined scenario.

vocab.def: Data collected about a system and sent for observation.
The portion of a resource currently being used.
A defined level at which attention or a different response may be needed.

sections.heading: Monitoring makes patterns visible
sections.body: Synthetic telemetry might show temperature, CPU utilization, memory use, storage use, power status, and network status. One reading is a clue; a trend and context often provide more information.

sections.heading: Labels depend on context
sections.body: A classroom scenario can label a reading normal, warning, or critical using its stated thresholds. Those labels are not universal rules for every piece of equipment.

sections.heading: Interpret, do not operate
sections.body: Use a provided dashboard or table. Do not connect to production monitoring, change thresholds, or take action on real infrastructure. Escalate uncertain results to an instructor.

practice.prompt: A synthetic dashboard shows normal temperature, warning storage, and critical network status. Which issue would you investigate first, and what context would you record?

quiz.question: What is telemetry?
options: Data collected about a system for observation
quiz.answer: Data collected about a system for observation

lab.objective: Classify synthetic telemetry using scenario-specific thresholds and record reasoning.

reflectionPrompt: Why should a monitoring label always be read with its equipment and scenario context?
